reason: Selected component ablation supports testing graph-distance context pruning, with single-framework and task-subset boundaries.

candidates.title: Compare distance-aware pruning for localization context
candidates.rule: When a repository-localization agent accumulates search results, compare graph-distance-aware context pruning with retaining all retrieved context under the same search workflow.
candidates.finding: On SWE-bench Common, removing pruning lowers function match rate from 76.34% (71 cases) to 72.04% (67 cases). The full framework also changes scheduling and search decomposition, which are separate interventions.
models: Claude-based OrcaLoca localization setup; exact version not established in inspected sections
candidates.conditions: The framework builds a repository/commit-specific graph; context management uses graph relationships.
candidates.limitations: Small ablation subset and no inspected confidence intervals. Graph reconstruction and distance computation add overhead; fine-tuning open models and other languages are future work rather than demonstrated portability.
candidates.validation_test: Compare pruned and unpruned contexts with identical search actions and token budgets; measure lost relevant evidence, localization precision/recall and complete repair success.
